headline: Asana's AI agents share memory across your company — but not your secrets
summary: Asana's new Agentic Work Management (AWM) product treats AI as coachable teammates, leveraging its 18-year-old Work Graph to enable shared memory and context awareness while maintaining strict data governance.
details: Enterprise AI agents often struggle with memory, forgetting previous interactions and failing to learn from past tasks. Asana's Chief Product Officer, Arnab Bose, revealed how the company tackled this by building Agentic Work Management (AWM) on top of their existing Work Graph architecture, treating AI agents as collaborative teammates rather than simple assistants.

The Work Graph, an 18-year-old foundation, organizes company information through a 'Pyramid of Clarity,' connecting tasks to projects, projects to portfolios, and portfolios to company-wide goals. This provides a real-time ledger of work, enabling AWM's AI agents to access overarching company objectives and share memory with human colleagues.

Unlike standard AI copilot tools that are stateless and tied to individual prompts, AWM's integration with the Work Graph allows AI agents to view company goals, update project statuses, and maintain a shared memory. This means an agent can recall past interactions and context, making it a more effective team member.

AWM is already in production with several successful enterprise customers, including FedEx, which has published a case study on its implementation. This indicates the product is meeting real-world needs for scalable AI agent deployment.

A critical challenge addressed by AWM is data governance. The system ensures that an AI agent's shared memory, built from workflows and feedback, does not leak confidential project context to unauthorized employees. Strict access controls differentiate between memory creation and task execution.

AWM also features dynamic model routing to simplify prompt engineering for users. For complex tasks like drafting a job description, the system automatically selects appropriate AI models, from powerful frontier models like Anthropic's Opus or OpenAI's GPT-4 to lighter, faster models for simpler requests.

To ensure commercial viability and predictable costs, Asana implemented a static cost per task completion for AWM. This billing abstraction absorbs the complexity of dynamic model selection and computational costs, preventing unpredictable credit burn rates that could lead customers to limit AI agent usage.
